statement.p: Parameterize the plane through the point (5, 1, 3) with the normal vector \left\lt 1,3,1\right>

p.em: (Use s and t for the parameters in your parameterization, and enter your vector as a single vector, with angle brackets: e.g., as \lt 1 + s + t, s - t, 3 - t \gt.)

static.solution:
\vec v_1 and \vec v_2 that are parallel to the plane. Such vectors are perpendicular to the normal vector to the plane, \vec n = \left\lt 1,3,1\right>. We can choose any vectors \vec v_1 and \vec v_2 such that \vec v_1\cdot \vec n = \vec v_2\cdot \vec n = 0.
One choice is \vec v_1 = \left\lt -3,1,0\right>, \qquad \vec v_2 = \left\lt -1,0,1\right>.
Letting \vec r_0 = \left\lt 5,1,3\right>, we have the parameterization \vec r(s, t) = \vec r_0+ s\vec v_1+t\vec v_2 = \left\lt 5-3s-t,1+s,3+t\right>.
